One Man's Trash is almost a good incremental game, but doesn't quite get there. The game is clearly trying to expand on Game About Digging a Hole, but doesn't understand the balance that game struck to keep it engaging for its short runtime.

Upgrades are tiny and lack impact. You often don't feel the effect of anything you're buying until you've accumulated several power-ups and realize "oh yeah, this IS slightly better." The game is also too long given the lack of variety. Given the game's roughly 5 hour runtime, the upgrades and progression systems needed to have new and interesting mechanics drip fed throughout the game. Unfortunately, what you see in the first 5 minutes is all you're going to get, and those upgrades are pretty basic. Something like movement upgrades would have been appreciated, since movement is clunky and terrain collision is wonky.

An effective incremental game repeatedly gives you a troublesome hurdle and dangles the solution just out of reach for you to pursue. You eventually obtain that solution and it's supposed to provide brief satisfaction until the next obstacle comes along and restarts the gameplay loop. This game does a well enough job at presenting the challenges, but the payoffs are rarely satisfying enough to drive the game's momentum forward.

掘りゲーとして期待している人にはおすすめしない。
理由は以下の通り。

■掘りに専念したい、無心で掘りたいのにそうさせない仕様がいくつかある
　1)パワー、範囲などの各種アップグレードには限界があり、ティアを上げる必要がある。（ティア上げ用の金がかかる）
　2)このゲーム、「掘る」というより「吸う」が正しいのだが、闇雲に吸っていると帰還できずに詰む可能性がある（ロープのレベルを常に意識）
　3)HPがあるため、落下死する可能性あり（自動で徐々に回復するが）
■バグがある
　勝手にゆっくりと下を向いてしまう現象が頻繁に発生する。
　タブキーを押して一時中断して復帰すれば戻るのだが、これに気づくまでポインタが勝手に動くので面倒だった。
■ボリュームは少ない
　ボリュームが少ないから面倒な仕様にしたのではないかと疑うくらいに少ない。
　クリアするだけなら160m掘ればエンディングに到達可能。

掘りゲー初心者にはおすすめしない。まずは別ゲーから入ったほうがいい。

Will another man's accidental discarded waste become your ticket to the big leagues? Grab your vacuum cleaner and find out.

Very reminiscent of A Game About Digging a Hole, except I liked this one more, One Man's Trash is a "holeslike", a game about trying to dig as deep as humanly possible while selling items and buying upgrades. You've purchased a junkyard where someone accidentally threw away a bitcoin harddrive and attempt to dig your way down, while collecting various items and upgrades along the way. Where this game improves on the original trendy indie, is in mostly the little things. You have all of the essentials you'd expect, like collecting low-value items at first and selling them at a loss while trying to get an upgrade or two, and will gradually improve your tool of choice, a vacuum cleaner, increasing its suction speed, spread, bag capacity, etc. Where it differs is the item collection and display feature, as you'll be collecting junk instead of ore this time, coming in a wide assortment of random landfill items to clean up and show off in your trailer. Home appliances, vehicles, paintings, statues, collectable merchandise, power tools, you name it. You're also able to build using the dirt you suck up, letting you shape your environment a little more neatly and form staircases back up. Other surprises come in the form of microbiomes and even some hostile creatures in the depths, so be wary..

游戏刚更新了难度选择。最简单的一档玩起来节奏很不错。刚开始可能还有点蒙，上手以后操作起来就很快了。以绳子为中心向下挖掘。吸尘器满了或者背包满了就爬绳上去卖吸到的东西。拉着绳子往下掉的时候会因为加速度越掉越快。一下子撞到平面容易掉血。如果在快触地的时候按跳跃键，稍微的往上爬一下，就可以避免落地扣血的情况。
	
	吸尘器有力量、大小、容量和范围四个维度可以升级。单看字面意思可能不太能理解，不过游戏贴心的在旁边添加了悬浮注释。背包空间和绳索长度也可以升级。灯具是可回收的消耗品，5元一个，不会涨价，便宜又实用。放在地底下会有紫色，绿色，白色等随机灯色。漂亮又不会太刺眼，灯光颜色差分也让我们不太容易迷路。扫描仪是找收集品用的，150一个，在前期有点贵。后期钱多了可以随便买。使用后显示出扫描范围内的隐藏物品的位置和距离。特殊的收集品和道具还有对应的颜色标识。如果要找缺少的收集品的话应该能派上大用场。
	
	游戏地形也设计的很不错。浅层的地方会碰到汽车和火车。这么大的东西当然不能整个吸走卖掉，但是车座和车厢里藏了不少的道具。再往下可以找到矿坑。每个矿坑里都有连好线的炸药可以炸。再往下会有一看到一个泥土像是水管一样横着交叠的区域，初见的时候虽然黑黑的一片，但在星星点点的道具光的照射下还是很震撼。不过我第一次掉下去没能上来。好在游戏可以通过让吸尘器过热或者掉落伤害来死亡重生。这块地方的底下有一个超大的飞行器。太大了，我在旁边挖了一会就没有管它。继续往下挖挖到了一处岔路多的隧道。挖着挖着居然挖到了一个地形看起来像是石洞一样的地方。被星星点点的荧石映照着，非常的好看。上面一层看到的飞行器的驾驶舱头居然就在这里，真的是巨大无比呀。这块地方的土堆上居然有游戏主角想要找的比特币！功夫不负有心人啊，居然真的找到了。
	
	总之游戏是挺好玩的。找到了比特币就变得超级有钱了。但是游戏没有结束依然可以继续往下挖。绳子没了继续往下挖，[spoiler]可以挖到中空的底哦。然后又从天上降落到垃圾场把唧一下摔死。[/spoiler]普通模式会在底下深处碰到虫子，困难模式没有可以向上攀爬的绳子。应该还是挺有挑战性的。

From Jony Pazu Games, One Man’s Trash is out now on PC/Steam. This is the second title being released and self-published by Jony Pazu Games, the first being Raiders of the Apocalypse.

You have used every cent you own to purchase some land that has somewhere buried beneath the ground a Hard Drive with $100,000,000 Bitcoin cryptocurrency within the storage. Inspired by the true story of a man who accidentally threw away 8,000 Bitcoin.

The premise is simple: you have a vacuum cleaner and need to begin collecting dirt and items you find, then sell them on Junkbay using your laptop. You have limited storage space for the items you collect, ranging from traffic cones and garbage bags to Uranium and Gold. Additionally, you have limited space within your vacuum for dirt, but both can be upgraded through Junkazon on your laptop using the funds earned from selling junk.

I must say, they have found a way to keep your progress within a limit, so you don’t focus too much on any one area. This is done by a progress bar, which levels up a membership to collect, so each stat will level to a limit until you must purchase a license upgrade.

You begin with a squared-off area with a rope lowered into the center with a crane. This will become your primary mode of transportation as you delve deeper into the dig. This is also behind an upgrade, which you will need to purchase to make longer on each upgrade.

This has its hazards and is all down to how you tackle your dig, as you will need to leave some dirt to get back out of the pit. As I discovered on my OCD run of clearing all the dirt as you get deeper.

You will leave behind broken paths and falling hazards that can be fatal. During your dig, you will come across items for use, such as sandwiches to heal, vouchers to decrease the cost of purchasing or increase the price of selling, and other consumables. For the satire of the game, you will also come across whoopee cushions to help you jump higher with a chuckle-inducing fart sound. Among the items to collect are collectables that have nods to popular culture, one of my favourites is a Pulp Fiction reference.

Around the area for the dig, you have units with pedestals to display your collectables, the amount of trash found, and cosmetic upgrades for your vacuum cleaner. So, for completionists, this is a great way to track your progress. You will encounter an enemy type as you get low enough, along with some unusual sights, so the game gets a bit deeper (see what I did there?) with hints to a story and an amazing discovery. Once you find the hard drive, you are given two choices: the cryptocurrency you were searching for or a mystery box. I

chose the mystery box, and the game expanded with more to do. I do apologise for the vagueness in some parts of the story and enemy types, but it was a nice surprise and eerie to boot, and I do not want to give spoilers. I managed this in just over four hours of gameplay. If you find yourself dying in-game due to attacks from that mystery enemy or from a fall, you will respawn at the top and lose all inventory items you have collected for good.

Graphically, it is vibrant and hints at a cartoon style, fitting in with the satire aesthetic. It looks great for an indie game and effectively portrays everything it needs to, from the physics of sucking up dirt and watching it diminish satisfyingly, to when you can use the vacuum cleaner to blow, so in theory, a build mode to create ledges and paths.

The soundtrack features a diverse array of comic acoustic guitar riffs with a jaunty feel. With the sounds of the vacuum cleaner being clear and crisp. You will hear this sound effect a lot. But within the options, you have the usual abilities to lower sound, vacuum, and music in-game.

Controls on PC revolve around the WASD with the mouse. There are not many controls to remember, but they still add enough to make the game feel immersive. The Steam page, at the time of this writing, states that it does not support controllers, but I found that my Xbox Series X controller worked well. The option screen displays the button configuration for controllers, so I’m guessing this may be an oversight. Once they are satisfied, it will be changed on release.

I found the keyboard and mouse to be more precise and easier to adjust for small pieces of dirt or unusual angles. However, the controller works fine, but you may need to adjust the sensitivity, as it seems a little slow by default.

I enjoyed this game; it’s not overly complicated and makes for a great time-eater. I found myself losing track of time while exploring and clearing the areas to uncover hidden secrets. With great nods to popular culture, a lovely artistic style, and general good fun, I could recommend it to many. One Man’s Trash is a great Indie game with enough to make you want more.

So while I've played "A Game About Digging A Hole", I was excited to play this game as thoroughly enjoyed it. However, was met with some things that have ultimately made me decide to give it a bad review. Here's why:

Things I enjoyed:
- The different coloured lights made a neat looking kaleidoscope when climbing up and down using the rope
- Immediately starting off with a vacuum, instead of dealing with pesky little dirt spots (I played the game where I left no spot unturned as I descended down)

Things I didn't like/annoyed me:
- Having absolutely no way of buying health, the amount of times I had died on my way back up to sell my stuff (including super rare items that only spawn once) and having to relying on RNG of getting a sandwich to spawn. When you have no control over how high you "soar" coming back up to the surface and taking damage, and then me going AFK for 5 minutes to let my health slowly refill is just a waste of time when I could be purchasing health (thus promoting the premise of the game further by needing to look for more stuff to sell) is something I'm shocked isn't in the game.  
- Only being able to hold two "rare" items, I should be able to hold more than one sandwich or whoopee cushion to help me progress in the game. 
-The worms - oh my goodness how annoying those were. Only being able to "dig" for 20 seconds and then hear the sound that another one was coming, and absolutely no way to deal with them - was infuriating. Only being able to fill up a quarter of my capacity on the vacuum cleaner or my inventory before trekking all the way back up to the surface made it meaningless to upgrade them in the first place, because the worms were just so dang consistent. 

I'm at the point where I'm simply going down as far as I can, not playing the game to its entirety to get through it. I was unaware that there would be jumpscare worms, as the game is not labelled as a horror type game, but to get scared by these pesky things and throw my gameplay off just made me re-install a similar game and go back and play through that. 

All in all, no, I would not recommend the game for what it's advertised as (a casual game that looked cozy enough where you weren't getting jumpscared every couple of minutes), and for the lack of things that I feel would improve overall gameplay.

Who Doesn’t Know the Game: “A Game About Digging A Hole”? The game where you simply dig holes in the yard of your newly bought house. The game we’re talking about today is based on that concept. This one is developed and published by Jony Pazu Games. Here’s our review of One Man’s Trash.

[b] First Impressions[/b] 
I’ll be honest. When I saw the game in my inbox, I thought, here we go again… Another game based on a popular title, another developer trying to milk the concept. But One Man’s Trash really surprised me in a good way. It’s a game that gets repetitive after about an hour, but the urge to keep playing is ridiculously strong. Even when I thought, ugh, I’m getting bored of this, I had to keep going, “just 10 more minutes.” Those 10 minutes turned a one-hour session into three hours.

[b] What You Actually Do[/b] 
In this game, you dig up junk and sell your trash via a platform called JunkBay. With that money, you buy upgrades to improve your gear. You’ve got character upgrades: Strength, Size, Capacity, and Range. And you’ve got gear and inventory upgrades: Inventory Space, Lamps, Rope, and Scanners. At some point, though, your upgrades get locked. You need to buy a higher tier first, sometimes costing around 20,000 dollars. Only after purchasing that tier can you continue upgrading. I actually think this is a clever idea, because it keeps you grinding for more money, which makes the game feel less repetitive. Oh, and you can also gamble in-game. There’s a slot machine where you can blow all your hard-earned cash. And why are you doing all this? Because you’re hunting for a lost crypto wallet. A lost hard drive worth millions. Funny enough, this reminds me of a real story. When I checked the Steam page, I actually read this: “Inspired by the true story of a man who accidentally threw away 8,000 Bitcoins.”

[b] Weird Stuff You’ll Find[/b] 
The game is full of surprises and strange mysteries. You’ll come across pop culture relics and unsettling secrets while vacuuming your way through the dirt. From toilets and traffic cones to old relics, lost consoles, cursed cartridges, and mythical collectibles. Need to get back up? Use your rope, or switch your vacuum cleaner to “spit” mode. What I really like is that the deeper you go, the weirder it gets. You’ll encounter stranger and stranger things, and yes, even creatures. I’m not telling you what exactly, because that would ruin the surprise. But trust me, you’ll be amazed.

[b] Final Thoughts[/b] 
This is one of those games that seems like it would get boring fast, but somehow you just keep wanting more. Think about mining in Minecraft. You’re deep in a cave, you know you should head back to the surface, but something inside you whispers, keep going, keep digging, keep exploring. That’s exactly the feeling this game gives you.

[b] Target Audience: [/b] Those Needing Stress Relief/Liking Simple Task Games [I] [/i]

[b] Summary: [/b]  

One Man's Trash is one of those games where you will play it, enjoy it, have a good time, but not remember in a few years. Which is perfectly fine: the game's low cost yet relaxing gameplay that has some good elements of discovery does the job in being engaging and yet not overly frustrating. There are times the game will change the formula enough to keep your interest, and the lightning system does well in strategic placement being rewarded without being too overly complicated/necessary. Granted, the game isn't going to blow you away in any one area, and the fact is that if you're looking for longetivity in gameplay, you're not going to get it here.

A lot of my complaints are little things that do add up at times. The reward system for your vaccum heads just lacks any pizzaz, and the game does have a visual style that doesn't draw the eye. The sound design is extremely lacking: games like this are really enhanced by immersive/appropriate sound elements (like the right sound for vaccuming up a specific material could have really done a lot). I did want more content in the big picture, but I do think the game is priced appropriately.

If you're looking for a game that you can relax to, this is up your alley. Just don't expect that much depth
